My land is in Quzhou. My mother grew wheat and corn here. Her mother did too. I will do the same — winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same plots. I have about 5 mu of flat irrigated land. That is what I can manage at my age alone.

For the wheat, I plant in October after the maize comes off. I buy seed from the village supply station — the improved kind they stock there, the kind my neighbors use. I do not save seed anymore because the station seeds do better. I apply the compound fertilizer at planting the way I always have, then add urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray once for weeds in early spring and once more when I see rust or aphids coming.

After wheat harvest in June I go straight into maize. I use hybrid seed, the small bags they sell at the station — everyone uses those now. Maize gets more nitrogen because it eats more. I irrigate twice if the summer rains are poor, which they usually are. I spray for corn borer and apply herbicide once after emergence.

For tillage I use the rotary machine I hire from the village — ploughing is too hard and costs more.

I expect about 420 jin of wheat per mu and maybe 520 jin of corn. Some years more, some less. That is what I plan for.
